items.headline: Second Life for Broken Gear
items.body: FIE: the Takamatsu City World Cup (Japan, Oct 15–18, foil) hosts the first broken-blade collection at an official FIE event, feeding Kazuyasu Minobe's Re-blade 2028 project (blades into knives, medals, keychains). USA Fencing profiled Joshua Au's ReCord Initiative: 334 body cords repaired and given free to nonprofit clubs and public schools (goal 500); recipients pay shipping; Absolute Fencing provides collection bins at tournaments. Source gives no age/home club for Au.

claim_check.claim: Off-strip/floor touch in épée is disregarded where floor not insulated
Touch on the conductive strip registering is annulled
Validity of a hit is a point of fact; no appeal except video review
Appeal allowed on misapplied rule; Head Referee settles; must be made by fencer, immediately, before next touch
Unjustified appeal on point of fact is penalized (Group 1, yellow card)
Bout Committee may intervene in disputes but cannot overturn a point of fact
Only the fencer on the strip may request video review; referee's decision final after review
National tournaments: replay guaranteed from R16 (Div I/Jr/Cdt Elite) or R8 (Challenger, Y10-Y14, Vet, etc.); teams gold/bronze; not pools

items.headline: Vet Worlds, part two: U.S. women's epee medals in Tbilisi
items.body: Follow-up to No. 2's men's item. Veteran World Championships women's individual epee, Tbilisi (per FIE posts Oct 12–13): Leslie Marx (USA) won Veteran 50 women's epee — FIE says her first title in that event since 2017. Veteran 40: Cassandra Bates (USA) silver, losing the final 10-9 to Julia Ashchuk; Lacey Biniak (USA) bronze. Veteran 70: Charlotta Bowie (USA) bronze; Astrid Kircheis (GER) defended her title (her 19th World Veteran medal). Field sizes not captured. Rewatch on FencingTV.
